title: Proof-Ledger for Tenant Isolation with Automated Residency Assertions
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Build an auditable, tamper-evident proof ledger and automated evidence generation pipeline that proves tenant workload residency and isolation for Dedicated capacity customers. The system should produce signed residency assertions and isolation summaries (per-tenant bundles) on a periodic cadence and on-demand, exportable to standard compliance bundles (PDF + JSON) and a machine-readable S3 artifact store. This ticket covers the core ledger format, assertion signing, retrieval API, and evidence exporter; integrations with the Compliance Console UI and long-term archival will be handled by follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Ledger entries capture node_id, tenant_id, region_tag, instance_fingerprint, boot_timestamp, config_hash, and routing_policy_version
Each assertion bundle is signed with the platform KMS key and includes verifiable metadata (signature, signing-key-id, generation_timestamp, build_id)
API to request on-demand residency assertion for a tenant within 30s and return a signed bundle URL
Automated nightly export writes per-tenant bundles to customer-churn-proof S3 path with immutability tags and retention metadata
Produce a human-readable PDF summary and a machine-readable JSON bundle for each assertion
Unit and integration tests for ledger write/read, signature verification, and exporter success path
design_notes: Ledger model: append-only WAL stored in cluster-controlled Postgres table + optional periodic snapshot to object store for long-term retention
Use existing KMS keyring (kms-prod/residency) to sign assertion bundles; include a rotating signing-key-id field to support key rotation audits
Leverage routing metadata already emitted by agent heartbeats to derive instance_fingerprint; do not rely on IP-based proofs alone due to NAT and cloud elastic IP churn
Export format schema: v1 with fields {bundle_id, tenant_id, region, entries[], signature, signing_key_id, generation_ts, verifications[]}, documented in Confluence
Use short-lived presigned URLs for bundle retrieval and an internal caching layer for repeated requests to reduce load on storage
Non-goal: This ticket does not implement UI visualizations or cross-tenant aggregations; those will be separate work items
rollout_plan: Feature branch -> integration tests against testbed dedicated cluster
Canary: enable ledger writes for 5 pilot tenants in eu-west-1 and us-west-2 for 48 hours
Smoke checks: verify signed bundle can be verified using public signing-key metadata endpoint
Gradual ramp: enable nightly exports and API endpoints for all Dedicated tenants in staged regions over two weeks
Post-rollout: 1-week monitoring window; alert on export failures >1% or assertion request latency >3s
security_considerations: Signing keys must remain in KMS, only signing performed by dedicated signing-service with enforced mTLS
Bundle retrieval requires tenant-scoped authorization and short-lived presigned URLs; bundles will never be public-by-default
Retention metadata must be honored by lifecycle policies to satisfy legal holds; exporter adds hold flag to object metadata when requested by legal/compliance
Protect against replay/fabrication by including monotonic ledger sequence numbers and node-signed heartbeat evidence in each entry
Require security review before enabling export to customer-managed buckets (due to cross-account risks)
